findings.claim: The mask in the timestamp writer was changed from 0xffffffff00000000 to 0x00000000ffffffff. That inverts the timestamp32 vs timestamp64 selection. Timestamp32 is now chosen when the low 32 bits (seconds) are zero, not when the high 32 bits (nanoseconds and upper seconds) are zero. For a nonzero-seconds, zero-nanosecond DateTime, the encoder now takes the 8-byte timestamp64 path. For a DateTime with seconds==0 but nanoseconds>0, the 6-byte path is taken, which writes only the low 32 bits of data64, so the nanoseconds are silently dropped. The result is corrupted timestamps on serialization, and it is unrelated to this feature.

receipt_plan.detail: Serialize DateTime values such as 1970-01-01T00:00:00.5Z and 2020-01-01T00:00:00Z with MessagePackWriter.Write(DateTime), then read them back. Round-trip equality fails for the first. Also byte-diff the output between base and head: the format code and length differ (0xd6 vs 0xd7).
